name: Perform the paramedical exam
sector: medical laboratory and health services (insurance medical evidence)
summary: A paramedical exam gives a life insurer measured evidence about an applicant's health: a medical history questionnaire, height, weight, blood pressure and pulse, blood and urine specimens and sometimes a resting ECG. A mobile health professional, usually a contractor paid per visit, phones the applicant to book, visits the home or workplace, obtains signed consent, collects the evidence into ePara and ships the specimen kit to the laboratory, while office coordinators chase unbooked assignments, no-shows and incomplete files. Most elapsed time is spent reaching the applicant and waiting for a convenient appointment; no-shows, failed draws and missing items send cases back for another call or visit.

baseline.org_archetype: The insurance medical evidence business line of a large Canadian laboratory company with a national network of about 60 employed and more than 1,200 contracted mobile health professionals.
baseline.notes: Starts when an examiner has accepted an assignment from the order desk and ends when the paramedical file is completed and the specimen kit shipped, or the order is closed. Laboratory testing and the final file review are separate processes.

trigger: An exam assignment accepted by a health professional appears in the health professional app.
end_state: The paramedical file is transmitted and matched to the order, the specimen kit is with the courier and the visit record is created for examiner pay, or the order is closed because the applicant withdrew, refused or could not be reached.

volume.seasonality: Follows insurance sales: busier in the first quarter and autumn, quieter in summer and late December; exams dropped in spring 2020 when in-person visits paused and insurers widened non-fluid limits.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map (12,000 to 21,000 a month), itself an estimate; seasonality is the author's estimate.

roles.title: Contracted mobile health professional (paramedical examiner paid per visit)

evidence.note: The organisation file treats the 1,200+ contracted examiners as an outside party, not a role, so this role is added. Examiners are phlebotomists, nurses and similar professionals (hh2012). Per-visit fees and mileage are converted to an hourly equivalent near the employed examiner's loaded cost; no published Canadian fee was found. FTE: about 78 percent of the examiner hours implied by volume (about 2.2 hours per exam including calls and travel), spread over several hundred part-time contractors.

Employed examiners do about 20 to 25 percent of exams following exactly the same steps; for the simulation the employed and contracted examiner roles should be pooled for the examiner steps, which are attributed to the contracted role. 55 of the 60 employed examiners. Wage near the Job Bank 33101 Ontario median; Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Case coordinator (insurance orders and examiner assignment)
roles.department: Insurance order desk and case management

evidence.note: Coordinators follow up unbooked assignments, rebook no-shows and chase incomplete files; FTE estimated from about 3 minutes per exam. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).
Network managers review examiner quality issues on about 1 to 2 percent of exams; estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Insurance Order Management System with Paraweb ordering and iCARE status hub
ePara electronic medical evidence collection on examiner laptops
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
Health professional portal and phone app (assignments, schedule, status)

steps.name: Review the assignment and check supplies
steps.description: The examiner opens the new assignment in the health professional app, reads which requirements the insurer ordered (paramedical questionnaire, vitals, blood profile, urine, resting ECG), notes fasting or language instructions and checks that the right insurer kit, urine cup and, if needed, the ECG machine and electrodes are on hand.

error.defect_description: Missing kit or ECG supplies not noticed until the visit.

evidence.note: Assignments displayed in the mobile ordering system; supplies on hand needed for a full schedule (dyn_hp). Wait reflects examiners checking the app between visits; estimate.

steps.name: Call the applicant to book the exam
steps.description: The examiner phones the applicant, confirms identity before naming the insurer, explains what will be collected, agrees a time and place (home or workplace, often early morning when fasting is required), tells the applicant how long to fast, to avoid alcohol beforehand and to have photo ID and the details of doctors seen in the last five years ready, asks about bigger cuff or scale needs, and records the appointment in the app.

error.defect_description: Fasting or preparation instructions not given, so the blood draw has to be redone or flagged non-fasting.

control.basis: Privacy procedure: confirm the applicant's identity before discussing the insurance application

next.condition: no answer or applicant asks for a call back

evidence.note: Company standard: client contacted within 24 to 48 hours of the order and booked within 72 hours subject to availability (dyn_para); preparation and fasting instructions (dyn_bro2018). Reach rate and call length are estimates.

steps.name: Log the attempt and try again
steps.description: The examiner records the attempt in the app, leaves a voicemail with a call-back number and tries again at a different time of day. When the 48-hour contact standard is about to pass without a booking, the assignment shows as unbooked on the office aging report.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Call backs are a common delay (wp2015); the 48-hour contact standard sets the escalation point (dyn_para). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Follow up an unbooked assignment
steps.description: From the daily report of assignments not booked within 48 hours, the coordinator calls the examiner for an update and phones the applicant from the office line, books the appointment directly if reached, reassigns the order to another examiner if the first one is overloaded, or asks the advisor for help.
outputs: booked appointment, reassignment or advisor request

error.defect_description: Appointment booked by the office conflicts with the examiner's schedule.

control.basis: Carrier service level: applicant contact within 24 to 48 hours and booking within 72 hours, monitored on the aging report

next.condition: advisor asked to help reach the applicant

evidence.note: Customer care representatives contact applicants (dyn_car); agents asked to remind clients after failed attempts (examone2021). Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the advisor to reach the applicant
steps.description: The advisor contacts the client and replies with a new number or a good time to call, or tells the office the client has withdrawn or chosen another insurer. The assignment waits on hold until then.

error.defect_description: The new number is also wrong.

next.condition: new number or call time supplied
client withdrew or no reply within the carrier limit

evidence.note: Author's estimate; unreachable applicants often have dropped the application.

steps.name: Confirm the appointment to the applicant and office
steps.description: The app sets the order to 'scheduled', which shows on iCARE for the advisor and insurer, and sends the applicant a confirmation by text or email with the time, the fasting instructions and a reminder the day before.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Confirmation and day-before reminders are standard vendor practice (examone2021); the company's OMS sends text and email confirmations.

steps.name: Prepare and confirm the visit the day before
steps.description: The day before, the examiner loads the order into ePara on the laptop, plans the route between the day's appointments and calls or texts the applicant to confirm the time and the fasting instruction. Applicants who now cannot make it are rebooked on the spot.

error.defect_description: Route planned with too little time between visits, making the examiner late.

next.condition: applicant cancels, is ill or asks for another day

evidence.note: Booking within 72 hours subject to client availability (dyn_para); the wait from booking to appointment (mode 2 days, up to a week) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel to the applicant's home or workplace
steps.description: The examiner drives from the previous appointment or home to the applicant's address with the kits, centrifuge if used, scale, blood pressure cuff and ECG machine. Travel time depends on the density of appointments; rural visits can take over an hour each way.

error.defect_description: None.

next.condition: applicant not home or turns the examiner away

evidence.note: Exams are done at the applicant's home or place of business (hh2012); travel times and the 8 percent no-show share are the author's estimates, no published rate was found.

steps.name: Verify identity and obtain signed consent
steps.description: The examiner checks the applicant's government photo ID against the order, confirms two identifiers, explains the exam and the tests, and has the applicant sign the insurer's authorization and the Notice and Consent and Chain of Custody section of the Lab ID slip, which permits collection, testing and release of results to the insurer. The examiner does not proceed if the applicant refuses or alters the slip.

error.defect_description: Identity or signature captured incorrectly, so the insurer cannot rely on the evidence.

control.basis: PIPEDA consent principle and the insurer's authorization: express written consent before collecting health information and specimens; laboratory practice of two-identifier checks

next.condition: consent given; vitals and fluids only

evidence.note: Client signs the Lab ID slip before any specimen is collected (dyn_para, dyn_kit2020); do not draw if the applicant declines to sign (crl_instr). Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Complete the medical history questionnaire
steps.description: The examiner reads the insurer's medical questions in ePara (conditions, treatments, medications, doctors, family history, tobacco, alcohol), types the answers and details such as dates and physician names, then has the applicant review and sign the declaration.

error.defect_description: Missing details such as dates, doctor names or medication doses.

evidence.note: Health history questionnaire is part of the paramedical (dyn_para, hh2012); 25 to 35 minutes for the whole paramedical. Split of minutes is an estimate.

steps.name: Measure height, weight, blood pressure and pulse
steps.description: The examiner weighs the applicant on a portable scale, measures height, takes the blood pressure and pulse after the applicant has rested, repeats the blood pressure when the first reading is high and records each reading in ePara.

error.defect_description: Single high reading recorded without repeats, or weight not on a level surface.

evidence.note: Vitals take 10 to 15 minutes including preparation (dyn_para). Blood ordered on about 90 percent of exams follows the organisation file's 15,000 specimen kits a month against 16,000 exams.

steps.name: Draw blood into the insurer kit
steps.description: The examiner records the time of the last food and drink, performs the venipuncture, fills the two or three tubes in the insurer's kit, labels them with the barcodes from the Lab ID slip and enters the insurer's lab code. The serum tube clots upright for 30 minutes and is centrifuged within 2 to 4 hours, then the serum is poured into the aliquot tube. A difficult draw may take a second attempt.

error.defect_description: Haemolysed, short-filled or mislabelled tube that the laboratory may reject.

control.basis: Laboratory specimen collection requirements (ISO 15189 pre-examination rules applied by the receiving laboratory): correct tube, fill and labelling

evidence.note: Blood profile 20 to 25 minutes with 2 to 3 vials (dyn_para); clotting and centrifuge timing and labelling (dyn_kit2020, crl_instr). Failed-draw share is an estimate.

steps.name: Collect and seal the urine specimen
steps.description: The applicant provides urine in the kit cup; the examiner checks and records its temperature, pours it into the labelled tubes and seals them with tamper-evident tape that the applicant signs and dates.

error.defect_description: Temperature not recorded or seal unsigned.

control.basis: Insurer and laboratory collection rules: urine with every blood kit, temperature recorded and tamper-evident seal signed by the applicant

evidence.note: Urine required with blood kits, temperature recorded, signed tamper tape, second appointment if the applicant cannot void (crl_instr); urine 10 to 15 minutes (dyn_para). ECG share is an estimate: several insurers have removed routine ECGs from their grids.

steps.name: Record a resting ECG
steps.description: The examiner asks the applicant to lie on a bed or couch, places the chest and limb electrodes, records the tracing on the portable ECG machine, checks it is free of artifact and attaches the tracing to the file or transmits it.

error.defect_description: Tracing with artifact or wrong lead placement that the reviewer rejects.

evidence.note: Resting ECG takes about 20 minutes and is done at home or office with a couch or bed (dyn_para).

steps.name: Review and submit the ePara file
steps.description: Before leaving or that evening, the examiner checks the file in ePara, which flags any required field left blank, completes missing answers, confirms all signatures are captured and transmits the file; for carriers still on paper the forms are scanned and uploaded.

error.defect_description: File submitted with an answer, signature or tracing missing.

control.basis: ePara built-in completeness edits and insurer documentation rules: required fields and signatures before transmission

evidence.note: ePara integrated quality control (dyn_hp); examiner apps alert to missing required fields (examone2016). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Match the submission and flag gaps
steps.description: The OMS matches the ePara file to the order, checks that every ordered requirement has a record (questionnaire, vitals, specimen barcode, ECG) and puts the order on a coordinator's exception list when something is missing or a specimen barcode does not match.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Automated matching of electronic submissions to orders is assumed for an OMS with ePara; share of exceptions handled at the next step is an estimate.

steps.name: Package and ship the specimen kit
steps.description: The examiner places the tubes in the clamshell with absorbent sheets, puts the laboratory copy of the authorization form in the bag pocket, seals it in the courier envelope with its own waybill and keeps it refrigerated at 2 to 8 C until the courier picks it up or it is dropped at a depot, within one day of collection. Sharps go to the examiner's own sharps container, never in the kit.

error.defect_description: Kit misses the courier cut-off or is shipped without the slip, risking a non-viable specimen.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods rules for exempt human specimens and laboratory instructions to ship within 24 hours

next.condition: OMS flagged a missing item or mismatch

evidence.note: Refrigerate at 2 to 8 C and ship within one day of collection by Purolator (dyn_kit2020); ship within 24 hours (crl_instr); specimens dropped off with a courier to the Brampton lab or the border (dyn_faq). The 7 percent exception share is an estimate.

steps.name: Record the completed visit
steps.description: The OMS sets the order to 'completed', posts the status to iCARE for the advisor and insurer, releases the paramedical file to the case review queue and creates the completed visit record that drives the examiner's per-visit pay.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: The carrier is notified as soon as the order is completed (dyn_para).

steps.name: Arrange a return visit for a missed specimen
steps.description: When blood cannot be drawn or the applicant cannot give urine, the examiner submits what was completed, notes the reason in ePara and books a second visit, usually for the whole kit, at a time the applicant chooses.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: If the applicant cannot void, arrange a second appointment for the entire kit (crl_instr). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Record a no-show
steps.description: The examiner waits about 15 minutes, calls the applicant, leaves a message or card, and records the no-show in the app so the office can rebook; the wasted trip is paid at a reduced fee or not at all, depending on the contract.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Rescheduling is a known delay (wp2015); wait time and pay rules are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase the examiner to fix a flagged file
steps.description: The coordinator works the exception list, calls or messages the examiner about the missing answer, signature, tracing or mismatched barcode, and has the examiner correct and resubmit the file; a missing specimen means a return visit.

error.defect_description: Correction applied to the wrong file.

next.condition: specimen missing or unusable; return visit
repeat or serious error by this examiner

evidence.note: Electronic forms reduce but do not remove incomplete submissions (examone2016); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Rebook after a no-show or escalate to the advisor
steps.description: The coordinator phones the applicant to rebook; after a second no-show or no reply, the coordinator notifies the advisor through iCARE and email, who decides with the client whether to continue.

error.defect_description: Rebooking not passed to the examiner.

next.condition: second no-show or no reply; advisor notified

evidence.note: Common practice; shares and waits are estimates.

steps.name: Review an examiner quality issue
steps.description: The network manager reviews the examiner's recent files and any complaint, records the issue, arranges coaching or retraining, and for repeated problems restricts assignments or ends the contract.

error.defect_description: None.

control.basis: Network quality program: monitoring of examiner errors and complaints under the examiner service contract

evidence.note: The organisation file says network managers monitor quality; process details are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Applicant hard to reach
exceptions.description: The examiner cannot book within 48 hours; the coordinator calls from the office, reassigns the order or asks the advisor for help, and some orders close unbooked.

exceptions.name: Applicant cancels the day before
exceptions.description: The day-before confirmation finds the applicant cannot make it and the visit is rebooked.

exceptions.name: No-show
exceptions.description: The applicant is not home or turns the examiner away; the trip is wasted and the coordinator rebooks or escalates to the advisor.

exceptions.name: Failed draw or applicant cannot void
exceptions.description: The examiner submits what was collected and books a return visit for the kit.

exceptions.name: Incomplete or mismatched submission
exceptions.description: The OMS flags a missing answer, signature, tracing or barcode mismatch and the coordinator has the examiner correct it.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from accepted assignment to file transmitted and kit shipped

evidence.note: Synthesis: the company contacts the applicant within 24 to 48 hours and books within 72 hours subject to availability (dyn_para), so most exams happen about 4 to 7 days after assignment; across 62 carriers an outstanding paramedical requirement takes 15.2 days on average from the carrier's view, which includes ordering delay and rebooking (ipipeline).

benchmarks.unit: minutes on site for a paramedical with fluids
business days from collection to results delivered to the carrier
benchmarks.population: Company insurance specimens tested in Canada

evidence.note: Downstream of this process; shows the specimen leg is short compared with booking.

pain_points.description: Reaching applicants and fitting the visit into their schedule takes most of the elapsed time; examiners and the office both make repeated calls.

evidence.note: Booking depends on client availability (dyn_para) and call backs are a known delay (wp2015).

pain_points.description: No-shows waste examiner travel and add a rebooking cycle.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; no published no-show rate was found.

pain_points.description: Non-fasting applicants, failed draws and applicants who cannot void lead to return visits.

evidence.note: Second appointment for the entire kit when the applicant cannot void.

pain_points.description: Kits that miss the courier cut-off sit overnight and, if delayed further, can become non-viable and need recollection.

evidence.note: Recollection of non-viable specimens (dyn_faq); refrigerate if not shipped the same day (crl_instr).

pain_points.description: Thin examiner coverage outside cities means long drives per visit.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the organisation file's note on rural coverage gaps.

sources.title: Paramedical services
sources.supports: Client contacted within 24 to 48 hours of the order and booked within 72 hours subject to client availability; paramedical 25 to 35 minutes (history questionnaire, height, weight, blood pressure, pulse); vitals 10 to 15 minutes; urine 10 to 15 minutes, 2 to 3 vials; blood profile 20 to 25 minutes, 2 to 3 vials plus urine; resting ECG about 20 minutes; stress ECG only at a fixed facility; fasting stated at booking; client signs the Lab ID slip before any specimen is collected.

sources.title: During the exam
sources.supports: The exam usually takes 25 to 35 minutes; health and family history questionnaire; height, weight, blood pressure and pulse; urine sample; blood drawn with standard laboratory equipment; fasting may be required; applicant signs an authorization slip before urine, blood and saliva samples.

sources.title: Health professionals
sources.supports: Mobile-friendly ordering system displays assigned paramedical appointments; health professionals enter and submit applicant information on laptops through ePara, whose integrated quality control is meant to ensure completion in one visit; a full schedule needs all supplies and equipment on hand and error-free sample collection.

sources.title: Insurance carriers
sources.supports: A Customer Care Representative identifies an available Health Professional and contacts the applicant; the Health Professional collects samples and applicant information, seals the samples and sends them to the laboratory; samples kept five weeks for repeat testing; ePara on tablet or laptop.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions: The model laboratory's insurance testing service order tracker
sources.supports: After collection specimens are packaged and dropped off with a courier to the Brampton laboratory or to the US border depending on the carrier's lab; average three business days from collection to results delivered to the carrier; non-viable specimens may need recollection.

sources.title: Insurance collections: specific instructions for examiners
sources.supports: Confirm applicant identity with at least two identifiers and verify picture ID; do not draw if the applicant declines to sign or alters the authorization slip; urine required with every blood kit and its temperature recorded; tamper-evident tape signed by the applicant; if the applicant cannot void arrange a second appointment for the entire kit; ship within 24 hours or the next shipping day and refrigerate until shipped.

sources.title: Hooper Holmes, Inc. annual report on Form 10-K for 2012
sources.supports: Paramedical exams by a network of phlebotomists, nurses, EMTs and other professionals; an exam typically consists of medical history questions, height, weight, blood pressure and pulse and blood and urine specimens tested by a laboratory; branch offices replaced by integrated customer service centres.

sources.title: Five days to issue (iPipeline analysis of outstanding requirements)
sources.supports: Across 62 life carriers the average collection time for an outstanding paramedical exam requirement is 15.2 days, with agent and insured named as responsible parties.

sources.title: Why does it take so long to get my policies issued?
sources.supports: Paramedical exams, blood draws and inspection calls are rescheduled or need call backs when clients are not prepared; advisors can reduce delays by telling clients what to expect.

sources.title: 5 key enhancements that move the life insurance exam process forward
sources.supports: Clients receive a reminder the day before the appointment; confirmation and reminder texts include cancel and reschedule options; agents are asked to remind clients when several contact attempts fail.

sources.title: Ask the experts: ensuring quality throughout the applicant exam process
sources.supports: Examiner app pre-populated from the order and health interview with about 70 percent of the lab slip pre-filled; app alerts examiners to missing required fields; specimens centrifuged immediately at service centres to avoid delayed-centrifugation errors.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 3: Consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Meaningful consent is required to collect, use and disclose personal information; express consent is generally required for sensitive information.

sources.title: Wages: Medical laboratory technical assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 26.25, high 36.00 dollars (Labour Force Survey 2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages: Medical administrative assistant in Ontario (NOC 13112)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 25.00, high 32.70 dollars (Labour Force Survey 2023-2024).

sources.title: Instructions for blood/urine kit (insurance)
sources.supports: Proposed insured reads and signs the Notice and Consent and Chain of Custody section and the tamper-evident seal; examiner completes the laboratory authorization form, labels tubes and enters the insurer lab code; urine temperature recorded, preservative tube minimum 7 mL; SST tube clots upright 30 minutes and should be centrifuged within 2 to 4 hours and serum poured into the aliquot tube; keep samples cool, store refrigerated at 2 to 8 C until courier pick-up; ship within one day of collection by Purolator in Canada.

sources.title: Everything you need to know about your insurance medical exam
sources.supports: A paramedical exam is 45 to 60 minutes at home or work; fasting may be required and the applicant is told so a morning appointment can be booked; up to 3 vials of blood, urine and possibly saliva in a sealed sterile kit; portable ECG if required; vitals-only service 10 to 15 minutes; reschedule if the applicant has a cold, flu or menses; avoid alcohol 24 to 48 hours before; bring photo ID and the contact details of health professionals seen in the last 5 years.

assumptions: Examiner steps are attributed to a contracted health professional role added with not_in_org_file, because the organisation file shows the 1,200+ contractors as an outside party. About 20 to 25 percent of exams are done by employed examiners following the same steps; a simulation should pool the two examiner roles for these steps.

The applicant booking call is made by the examiner, as in the organisation file's process description; the company's web pages also say a customer care representative contacts the applicant, which is modelled as the office follow-up step.
No published no-show, cancellation or failed-draw rates were found; 8 percent no-show, 12 percent day-before cancellation and about 6 percent return visits are the author's estimates.

Exam content shares (questionnaire 82 percent, blood 90 percent, ECG about 10 percent of exams) are estimates; the blood share follows the organisation file's 15,000 specimen kits against 16,000 exams.
Examiner hourly cost is an hourly equivalent of per-visit fees and mileage; no Canadian fee schedule was opened.
The wait from booking to the appointment (mode 2 days, up to 7) and overnight waits before visits reflect applicant availability, not examiner capacity.
Travel is counted once per visit (the leg to the applicant); the leg home at the end of the day is not counted.
